The current leader uses a trimmed mean on a small DWT pool, leveraging trend strength but potentially ignoring complementary models like ETS/THETA which showed stability in earlier windows. Given the unstable ranking (tau 0.212) and strong trend, testing the full pool with simple arithmetic mean is a robust baseline to see if diversity outweighs the specific DWT focus.
Test broad inverse-error weighting to handle ranking instability and correlated errors, compared against the robust trimmed_mean leader.
Test robust centroid combination on full pool to compare against trimmed mean on DWT subset.

The series has a very strong trend (0.926) but unstable ranking across windows, suggesting that trimming outliers or using a robust combiner on a high-quality subset is key. The current leader `a1` used a trimmed mean on the top 3 DWT models. I will now test a broader approach: a trimmed mean on the full pool to see if including more diverse models (while still being robust) helps, as the "robust" hint suggests resilience to individual model errors in this high-trend regime.

The current leader (a1) uses a trimmed mean on a small DWT subset. To test if robustness to the unstable ranking can be improved by leveraging the complementary error structures of different correlation groups, I will combine models from distinct clusters (DWTs for trend, ETS/THETA for seasonality, and RF/CatBoost for non-linearity) using inverse error weighting. This tests a "best-of-each-world" weighted approach against the robust trimmed mean on a homogeneous subset.

The current leader (a1) uses a trimmed mean on a small DWT subset. Since ranking stability is very low (tau=0.212), relying on a fixed top-3 subset is risky; a model that was #5 in one window could be #1 in the next. I will test a robust combination over the full pool using Caruana's forward selection weights, which adaptively determines model importance based on error correlation and magnitude, potentially capturing complementary information better than static trimming or simple inverse error weighting.

The current leader (a1) uses a trimmed mean on a small DWT subset. Since ranking stability is very low (tau 0.212), relying on a fixed small subset of top models is risky as the "best" model changes by window. I will test a robust combination over the full pool using the median, which naturally handles the instability and potential outliers better than a mean or trimmed mean without requiring arbitrary trim percentages.
Test robust trimmed mean on top-5 model pool to leverage complementary high-error models.

The series has a very strong trend (0.926) but unstable rankings across windows, suggesting that models capturing the trend differently may complement each other. The current leader uses a trimmed mean on a small DWT-focused pool. To test if a more robust statistical combination over a diverse set of top performers can beat this, I will use DBA on pool5 (which includes ETS/THETA for their strong recent performance and DWT models for trend).

The leader (a1) uses a trimmed mean on a small pool of 3 DWT models. To challenge this, I will test a robust DBA (Democratic Bagging/Aggregation) approach on the same tight pool of top-performing models, as DBA can sometimes outperform simple trimming when model errors are correlated but not identical.

The series has a very strong trend (0.926) but unstable ranking across windows, suggesting that models capturing the trend differently may complement each other. The current leader uses a trimmed mean on a small pool of DWT models. I will test an inverse_error weighted combination on this same top-3 pool to see if giving more weight to the best individual model (DWT_catboost) improves upon the equal-weighted robust average.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8758. Series context: trend strength 0.9261 and seasonal strength 0.3514; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.212); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.712.
